mainTopic: When שבת, תרומה, חצר and designation fix produce for מעשרות, especially according to רבי אליעזר, and רבי יוחנן's rule that only finished produce becomes fixed
overview: The גמרא challenges the idea that, for רבי אליעזר, designating fruit for tomorrow makes it fixed (קבע) for מעשר. It points out that רבי אליעזר holds that whenever leftovers can be returned, nothing is fixed, and it proves this from a משנה about olives taken from a vat. An attempt to answer by saying the eater is impure and cannot return the fruit fails, because the fruit never left its place. רב שימי בר אשי answers instead that רבי אליעזר holds even separating תרומה fixes produce, so שבת certainly does. The גמרא then tries to show that the חכמים agree, but rejects the proof: the explicit designation may be what fixed the fruit, and mentioning שבת teaches that טבל counts as prepared for שבת. A ברייתא about finishing a grape cluster seems to show רבי אליעזר saying שבת does not fix fruit. רבי נתן explains that he only meant the person may finish later, outside the חצר or after שבת. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that שבת, תרומה, חצר and מקח fix produce only when its processing is complete. Including שבת in that list rejects the lone view of הלל.

steps.title: But the leftovers go back to the pile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how designating fruit could make it fixed for מעשר, since רבי אליעזר holds that anything whose leftovers are returned is not fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't the leftovers go back to the pile? And we have heard that רבי אליעזר said: anywhere the leftovers go back, the food does not become fixed for tithing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that saying 'I will eat from here' makes the fruit fixed for מעשר. Whatever the person does not eat simply goes back, so why should anything be fixed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion assumed that, for רבי אליעזר, designating fruit fixes it for מעשרות. The challenge uses another known rule of רבי אליעזר: if the unused portion returns to the pile, the act does not fix the food. Since a person who designates fruit for tomorrow puts back whatever he does not eat, the two ideas seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: fixed it, made it a 'set' meal that requires מעשר
we have heard him say (we know his opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: Here קבע means fixing produce so that it now requires מעשר before eating. It does not mean a fixed time or schedule.

phrases.english: But isn't it true that its leftover returns [to the pile]?
And we have heard that Rabbi Eliezer said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּמוֹתָרוֹ חוֹזֵר — לָא קָבַע!
phrases.english: Anywhere its leftover returns, it does not become fixed [for tithes]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the preceding assumption (from the earlier part of the daf) that designation fixes the fruit for מעשר according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that, according to רבי אליעזר, designating fruit fixes it for מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר holds that returnable leftovers prevent קבע. Designated fruit is returnable, so designation should not fix it.

steps.title: Source: the משנה of olives from the vat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רבי אליעזר's rule from a משנה in מסכת מעשרות about eating olives taken from a vat.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Someone who takes olives from the vat may dip them one at a time in salt and eat them. If he dipped them and put ten in front of himself, he must tithe. רבי אליעזר says: from a pure vat he must tithe; from an impure vat he is exempt, because he returns the leftover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that serves as the source for 'where leftovers return, it is not fixed.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating olives one at a time is casual snacking, so no מעשר is needed. Setting ten olives in front of oneself counts as a fixed meal. רבי אליעזר adds a distinction: from an impure vat the eater is exempt, and he explicitly gives the reason 'because he returns the leftover.' That stated reason is the proof of his principle.

keyTerms.meaning: a vat where olives are stored to soften before pressing

steps.whyThisMatters: The words 'מפני שהוא מחזיר את המותר' are the exact source of רבי אליעזר's rule quoted in step 1.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: One who takes olives from the vat
may dip them one by one in salt and eat [without tithing].

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם טָבַל וְנָתַן לְפָנָיו עֲשָׂרָה — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: And if he dipped and placed ten before him, he is obligated [to tithe].

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִן הַמַּעֲטָן טָהוֹר — חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: From a pure vat, he is obligated;
from an impure vat, he is exempt,
because he returns the leftover [to the vat].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the rule of רבי אליעזר used in the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's principle that returnable leftovers prevent קבע
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת מעשרות: 'מן המעטן טמא פטור מפני שהוא מחזיר את המותר'

steps.title: Why do the two clauses differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion that asked what distinguishes the first clause of the משנה from the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What is different about the first clause, and what is different about the last clause?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reminds us that this משנה was analyzed elsewhere. It is setting up רבי אבהו's explanation, which will show exactly when leftovers count as 'returnable.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not obvious why the purity of the vat should matter for מעשר. The question asks for the practical difference between the cases. The answer will clarify the mechanism behind the 'returning leftovers' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: and we discussed it (an earlier analysis of this source)

phrases.english: And we discussed it:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא?
phrases.english: What is different in the first clause, and what is different in the last clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a clarifying question about the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference between the two clauses explains the different rulings

steps.title: First clause: a pure vat, so he cannot return the olives
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the first clause deals with a pure vat and an impure person, who cannot put the olives back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The first clause is a case of a pure vat and an impure person, who cannot put the olives back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו begins his answer by explaining the case where the eater must tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An impure person makes the olives he touches impure. If he put them back, he would make the whole pure vat impure, so he cannot return them. He therefore takes only what he plans to eat, and that act fixes the olives as a meal that requires מעשר.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said:
The first clause is with a pure vat and an impure person,
who cannot return it [the olives to the vat].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 for the first clause.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first clause is a pure vat with an impure eater. He cannot return the olives, so taking them fixes them for מעשר.

steps.title: Last clause: an impure vat, so he can return the olives
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the last clause deals with an impure vat and an impure person, who can put the olives back, so they are not fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last clause is a case of an impure vat and an impure person, who can put the olives back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו finishes his answer by explaining the case where the eater is exempt from מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vat is already impure, so returning the olives causes no harm. Because the eater knows he can put back whatever he does not eat, his taking them does not fix them. This confirms רבי אליעזר's rule: returnable leftovers mean no קבע, which supports the challenge in step 1.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, the key factor is whether the leftovers can be returned. If they can, as with olives from an impure vat, taking food does not fix it for מעשר. If they cannot, it does. This is why designating fruit for tomorrow seems unable to fix it, since its leftovers return.

phrases.english: The last clause is with an impure vat and an impure person,
who can return it [the olives to the vat].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אבהו's answer and confirms the principle behind the challenge in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The last clause is an impure vat with an impure eater. He can return the olives, so they are not fixed and he is exempt.

steps.title: Our משנה is also a pure storage area and an impure person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies רבי אבהו's answer to our משנה: it is a case of a pure storage area and an impure person, so the fruit cannot be returned and is therefore fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is also talking about a pure storage area and an impure person, who cannot put the fruit back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the opening question. It takes רבי אבהו's explanation of the משנה in מעשרות and uses it for our משנה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's rule is that fruit is not fixed if leftovers can be returned. If the person is impure and the storage area holds pure fruit, he cannot return the leftovers, because he would make the rest impure. So the fruit he designated would be fixed, and the question on רבי אליעזר goes away.

phrases.english: Our mishna too deals with a pure storage area
and an impure person,
phrases.notes: His touch would make the pure fruit in the storage area impure.

phrases.english: who cannot put it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי בְּמוּקְצֶה טָהוֹר וְגַבְרָא טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אבהו's case from the משנה in מעשרות to our משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה conflicts with רבי אליעזר's rule that returnable fruit is not fixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: In our משנה the person is impure and the storage area is pure, so he cannot return the fruit. It is therefore fixed.

steps.title: But the fruit is already sitting in its place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. In our case the fruit was never taken out of the storage area, so the issue of returning it does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they are already standing in place, as if returned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The olives in מעשרות were taken out of the vat, but here the person only stood by the storage area and spoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'cannot return it' reasoning only works if the fruit was removed. Here he never removed anything. The fruit he designated is still in the storage area, effectively already 'returned', so his impurity makes no difference. The question on רבי אליעזר is back.

keyTerms.meaning: Already standing in a returned state, still in place

phrases.english: But aren't they already standing returned!
phrases.notes: He never took the fruit out. He only declared what he would eat.

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that our משנה is a pure storage area with an impure person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being unable to return fruit only matters if it was taken out. Here it never left the storage area.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי: רבי אליעזר follows his own view
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי gives a new answer. רבי אליעזר holds that separating תרומה makes produce fixed, so שבת certainly does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב שימי בר אשי said: You are asking from רבי אליעזר? רבי אליעזר follows his own reasoning, since he says תרומה makes produce fixed, and all the more so שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier answer. רב שימי בר אשי explains that for רבי אליעזר, שבת itself makes produce fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'returnable leftovers' rule is not the deciding factor here. רבי אליעזר holds that even separating תרומה fixes produce, so שבת, which is stronger, certainly does. That is why designating fruit before שבת makes it fixed in other years.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
You are asking from Rabbi Eliezer?
Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning, for he said:
Teruma fixes produce, and all the more so Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר קָא אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the case to the speaker's own view (לטעמיה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's returnable-leftovers rule should mean the fruit is not fixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אליעזר, שבת fixes produce on its own, just as תרומה does.
steps.whyThisMatters: It answers רבא's question according to רבי אליעזר: שבת does fix produce. The next steps check what the חכמים hold.

steps.title: Source: רבי אליעזר says תרומה fixes produce
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that רבי אליעזר forbids snacking on produce once תרומה was taken, even before its work is finished. The חכמים permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: fruits from which תרומה was taken before their work was finished: רבי אליעזר forbids eating from them casually, and the חכמים permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב שימי בר אשי's claim about רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you may snack casually (אכילת עראי) on unfinished produce without tithing. רבי אליעזר says that once תרומה was separated, the produce is fixed and snacking is forbidden. The חכמים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Casual snacking, not a fixed meal
As we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'the חכמים permit' means they disagree with רבי אליעזר about תרומה. That does not yet tell us what they hold about שבת. The next step tries to find that out.

phrases.english: As we learned: fruits from which one separated teruma
before their work was completed,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹסֵר לֶאֱכוֹל מֵהֶן עֲרַאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer forbids eating from them casually,
and the Sages permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: פֵּירוֹת שֶׁתְּרָמָן עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר holds that תרומה makes produce fixed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת מעשרות (2:4) about fruit from which תרומה was separated before its work was completed

steps.title: Come and hear from the חכמים in the סיפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the חכמים in the סיפא of our משנה. They require marking the fruit and saying 'from here to there'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the latter clause: And the חכמים say: not until he marks the fruit and says 'from here to there'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new attempt to answer רבא's question, this time from the חכמים. Here it only quotes their words; the next step draws the inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים also hold that שבת fixes produce, the answer to רבא would not depend on רבי אליעזר's minority view alone. Their statement is the starting point for that inference.

phrases.english: Come and hear from the latter clause,
and the Sages say:
not until he marks it and says 'from here until there'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי אליעזר to the חכמים.
steps.raayaObject: That שבת fixes produce, even according to the חכמים

steps.title: Inference: in other years the fruit is forbidden because שבת fixes it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the leniency applies only in שביעית, when there is no tithing. In other years the fruit would be forbidden, apparently because שבת fixes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that it is ערב שבת in שביעית, when the fruit cannot be tithed. But in the other years of the cycle, when it can be tithed, it is forbidden. Why? Isn't it because שבת fixes it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the inference from the חכמים's words to answer רבא: שבת fixes produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks only about שביעית, when no מעשר applies. That implies that in other years, marking the fruit would not be enough to eat it untithed. The גמרא suggests the reason is that שבת itself made it fixed for מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh (Sabbatical) year, when no מעשר is taken
The other years of the seven-year cycle

phrases.english: The reason is that it is Shabbat eve in the Sabbatical Year —
which is not subject to tithing,
but in the other years of the cycle,
which are subject to tithing — they are forbidden.
What is the reason?
Is it not because Shabbat fixes them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the source quoted in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: שבת fixes produce for מעשר, even according to the חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied ruling about the other years in the חכמים's statement

steps.title: No: his marking is what fixed the fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The fruit is fixed because he marked it and said 'from here to there I will eat tomorrow', not because of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is different there. Since he said 'from here to there I will eat tomorrow', he has fixed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from the חכמים. It gives a different reason the fruit is forbidden in other years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clearly setting aside specific fruit for a meal is itself an act that fixes it for מעשר. So the ruling for other years can come from his declaration, and the proof that שבת fixes produce falls away.

phrases.english: No, it is different there,
since he said:
'From here until there I will eat tomorrow' —
he has fixed it.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the חכמים hold שבת fixes produce
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fixing can come from his explicit designation, not from שבת.

steps.title: If so, why mention שבת at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the declaration is what fixes the fruit, the same would be true on a weekday. So why does the משנה speak about שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why mention שבת specifically? Even on a weekday it would be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection it just made. If the declaration fixes the fruit, the משנה seems to have no reason to mention שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A declaration works the same on any day. So the משנה's focus on ערב שבת looks pointless unless שבת adds something.

phrases.english: If so, why mention Shabbat specifically?
Even on a weekday it would also be so!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the declaration, not שבת, fixes the fruit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the mention of שבת in the משנה would be unnecessary.

steps.title: שבת teaches that טבל counts as prepared for שבת
steps.stepSummary: שבת is mentioned to teach that טבל is considered prepared for שבת. If someone wrongly tithed it on שבת, it is tithed and may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that טבל is considered prepared for שבת: if someone transgressed and tithed it, it is tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the משנה mentions שבת. The case teaches a separate law about טבל on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think untithed produce is מוקצה on שבת, since you may not tithe it then. The משנה teaches that it still counts as prepared, so if someone tithed it anyway, it becomes permitted. So the mention of שבת is needed, and the rejection in step 12 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required portions have not yet been taken

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that שבת fixes produce for מעשר, a קל וחומר from תרומה. The proof that the חכמים agree was rejected, because explicit designation may be what fixed the fruit. The mention of שבת teaches that טבל is considered prepared for שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It brings in a separate rule: טבל is not מוקצה, and tithing it on שבת after the fact works.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that untithed produce is prepared with regard to Shabbat,
so that if he transgressed and tithed it — it is tithed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּטֶבֶל מוּכָן הוּא אֵצֶל שַׁבָּת
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new law explains the wording (הא קמשמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning שבת is pointless if the declaration fixes the fruit.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת is mentioned to teach that טבל is prepared for שבת, so tithing it after the fact works.

steps.title: A contradiction from the case of eating a grape cluster
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי אליעזר saying that a person eating grapes may finish, even after entering a חצר or after שבת begins. This seems to show that שבת does not fix fruit, which clashes with our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we raise a contradiction: If a person was eating from a cluster of grapes and walked from a garden into a courtyard, רבי אליעזר says he may finish eating, and רבי יהושע says he may not finish. If it got dark on Friday night while he was eating, רבי אליעזר says he may finish, and רבי יהושע says he may not finish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict our משנה. In the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר allows a person to keep eating untithed grapes even once שבת has started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you may snack on untithed fruit casually. But certain events, such as bringing it into a חצר or the start of שבת, 'fix' it so that it needs מעשר first. If רבי אליעזר lets the person finish the grapes on שבת, it seems שבת does not fix the fruit for him. That clashes with our משנה, which treats שבת as having an effect.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And we raise a contradiction': a ברייתא is brought that seems to clash with the משנה
A garden, where you may snack casually without separating מעשר
A courtyard; bringing fruit into it can fix the fruit for מעשרות
The point at which produce becomes 'fixed', so you can no longer snack on it without separating מעשר

steps.confusionAlert: Grapes in a cluster are usually meant to be pressed into wine, so their 'work' is not finished yet. Keep this in mind, because it becomes important in רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 17.

phrases.english: And we raise a contradiction:
If one was eating from a cluster of grapes,
and he came in from a garden to a courtyard,
Rabbi Eliezer says: he may finish,
Rabbi Yehoshua says: he may not finish.
If it grew dark on the night of Shabbat,
phrases.notes: That is, Friday night arrived while he was still eating.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: he may finish,
Rabbi Yehoshua says: he may not finish!
phrases.notes: The exclamation marks this as a challenge to our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב שימי בר אשי's claim (step 8) that for רבי אליעזר שבת fixes produce. It tests that claim against a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר seems to say שבת does not fix unfinished fruit.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי בר אשי's statement (step 8) that רבי אליעזר holds תרומה fixes produce, and all the more so שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר lets the eater finish the grapes on שבת itself, then שבת does not fix the fruit in his view. This contradicts רב שימי בר אשי's claim that for רבי אליעזר שבת fixes produce (a קל וחומר from תרומה).

steps.title: רבי אליעזר meant finishing outside the courtyard or after Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: Based on רבי נתן, the גמרא explains that רבי אליעזר never allowed finishing inside the חצר or on שבת. He meant the person may finish after leaving the חצר or after שבת ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is as it is taught: רבי נתן says, When רבי אליעזר said 'he may finish', he did not mean he may finish in the courtyard. Rather, he goes outside the courtyard and finishes. And when רבי אליעזר said 'he may finish', he did not mean he may finish on שבת. Rather, he waits until after שבת and then finishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by quoting רבי נתן's explanation of רבי אליעזר. 'He may finish' means later, not right now inside the חצר or on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only seemed to clash with our משנה because we read 'he may finish' as 'right away'. רבי נתן shows that רבי אליעזר agrees the person must stop eating inside the חצר or once שבת begins. He only holds that the fruit is not permanently fixed, so the person can resume later. So the ברייתא no longer contradicts our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There': referring to the other source, here the ברייתא
'As the reason is taught': the source itself spells out its explanation
The end of שבת, Saturday night

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not say the person may keep eating on שבת. He must stop. He only says the fruit is not permanently fixed, so eating can resume after שבת.

phrases.english: There, the reason is as it is taught:
Rabbi Natan says:
It is not that when Rabbi Eliezer said 'he may finish',
he meant he may finish in the courtyard,
but rather: he goes outside the courtyard and finishes.
And it is not that when Rabbi Eliezer said 'he may finish',
he meant he may finish on Shabbat,
but rather he waits until after Shabbat and finishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 15 by reinterpreting רבי אליעזר's words in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the contradicting source, based on an explicit explanation found in the ברייתא itself (רבי נתן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He may finish' meant right away, even on שבת or inside the חצר, so שבת would have no effect for רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'He may finish' means later: after leaving the חצר or after שבת ends. So רבי אליעזר agrees that שבת stops the casual eating, and there is no contradiction with our משנה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only finished produce becomes fixed
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that שבת, תרומה, חצר and מקח all fix produce for מעשרות only once the produce's processing is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: שבת, תרומה, a courtyard, and a purchase all fix produce for tithes only when the produce's work is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling from רבי יוחנן. It sets a condition on when the 'fixing' events actually work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four things that can make produce 'fixed' for מעשרות: שבת, separating תרומה, bringing it into a חצר, and buying it. רבי יוחנן adds a condition for all four: they work only if the produce is fully processed. Unfinished produce, like grapes still meant for pressing, is not fixed by any of them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When רבין came': רבין bringing a teaching from ארץ ישראל to בבל
The portion given to a כהן; separating it can fix produce for מעשרות
A purchase; buying produce can fix it for מעשרות
'Fix': make produce obligated in מעשר before it can be eaten
'Their work is finished': the produce's processing is complete

steps.whatToRemember: Four events fix produce for מעשרות: שבת, תרומה, חצר and מקח. According to רבי יוחנן, none of them works unless the produce is fully processed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for the laws of מעשרות. Being finished is a precondition for any of these events to fix the produce.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whether Shabbat, or teruma,
or a courtyard, or a purchase —
all of them do not fix produce for tithes,
except for an item whose work has been completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the contradiction about grape clusters, the גמרא brings a halachic rule that defines when the fixing events, including שבת, take effect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת, תרומה, חצר and מקח fix produce for מעשרות only when its processing is complete.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only fully processed produce can be fixed for מעשרות. Unfinished produce is not fixed by שבת, תרומה, a חצר, or a purchase.

steps.title: Why שבת is in the list: to exclude הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן included שבת in his rule to reject the opinion of הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: שבת: it is mentioned to exclude the view of הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through רבי יוחנן's list to show what each item adds, beginning with שבת. This line is a setup: it names whose opinion is being rejected, and the next line brings the source for that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said שבת fixes produce only if its processing is complete. Why say this about שבת specifically? Because someone holds that שבת fixes produce even when processing is not done, and that someone is הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to reject a different opinion
הלל הזקן, the great early sage
Completion of the produce's processing, which is needed before it can become fixed for מעשרות

phrases.english: Shabbat: it comes to exclude the view of Hillel,
phrases.notes: Explains why שבת appears in רבי יוחנן's list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the purpose of each item in רבי יוחנן's list from Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Including שבת in the rule teaches that, unlike הלל, שבת does not fix produce whose processing is unfinished.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing הלל's opinion
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי יהודה saying that הלל alone forbids eating fruit that was gathered for further processing once שבת began.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Someone is gathering fruit from place to place in order to cut it up, and the day became holy over it (שבת began). רבי יהודה said: הלל alone forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that הלל really holds this view. In the ברייתא's case, the fruit was still being processed when שבת arrived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fruit was not finished, since the owner still planned to cut it up. Even so, הלל forbids snacking on it without tithing, because he holds that the start of שבת fixes it. The word 'alone' tells us this is a lone view, and רבי יוחנן's rule rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
One who gathers or collects produce into a pile
And the day became holy over them, meaning שבת began
By himself, alone; הלל held this view on his own

steps.confusionAlert: 'הלל לעצמו אוסר' does not mean that הלל forbade the fruit only for himself personally. It means הלל was alone in forbidding it, against the other sages.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יוחנן's words 'only once processing is complete' were said on purpose, to reject הלל's view. In practice, the halacha does not follow הלל here.

phrases.english: as it is taught: one who gathers fruits
from place to place in order to cut them,
phrases.notes: The fruit still needs more processing, so it is not yet finished.

phrases.english: and the day became sanctified upon them,
phrases.notes: שבת began while the work was unfinished.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Hillel alone prohibits it.
phrases.notes: Only הלל holds that שבת fixes unfinished produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the opinion of הלל that Step 18 said was being excluded.
steps.raayaObject: That הלל holds שבת fixes produce for מעשרות even before its processing is complete.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה reports that הלל alone forbids fruit gathered for cutting once שבת began.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule that שבת fixes produce only once its processing is complete deliberately rejects הלל, who alone held that שבת fixes even unfinished produce.
